Employers and union reach proposed sector wage settlement

Media centre · Devran Pell
7 October

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria and the Food Production Workers Union have reached a proposed sector wage settlement following negotiations in Saltmarsh. The proposal is subject to approval by participating employers and union members.

The settlement would raise the adult production minimum from KRN 14.20 to KRN 14.85 an hour. It also provides for a 4 per cent increase in shift allowances and eight hours of paid job-related training per covered employee each year.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “The proposed agreement recognises the pressure on household budgets while giving employers a clear basis for planning. The training provision also addresses a shared concern about progression within factories.”

The federation has circulated the full terms to all 63 participating employers. Existing contractual rates above the sector minimum are addressed separately in the document. Current terms remain in force while the approval process takes place.

Federation publishes costing guide for proposed wage agreement

Media centre · Devran Pell
12 October

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has published a costing guide to help participating employers assess the proposed sector wage agreement. The guide accompanies the settlement terms circulated on 7 October.

Worked examples cover basic pay, shift allowances and paid training time. For an employee working 38 paid hours a week at the adult production minimum, the proposed hourly increase of KRN 0.65 would add KRN 24.70 to weekly basic pay.

The guide explains that this figure excludes overtime, allowances and employer contributions. It also asks businesses to account for training cover where production duties need to be reassigned during an employee’s eight annual paid training hours.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “Employers need to assess the whole agreement using their own staffing patterns. These examples provide a common starting point.” The proposal remains subject to approval, and the guide does not replace the full settlement document or individual employment contracts.

Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
9 October

Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy

Media centre · Mara Vennick
28 August

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

New labelling guidance needs clearer examples for small producers

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
3 September

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has asked the Food Standards Office to expand its draft guidance on ingredient labelling. Members say the document leaves uncertainty about how to display ingredients used within prepared fillings and sauces.

The federation reviewed 42 sample labels supplied by 18 manufacturers. Its technical team identified three recurring questions: where to place ingredient brackets, how to describe mixed oils and when a change in recipe requires revised packaging.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A bakery in Val-Brume should be able to reach the same answer as a sauce maker in Ostara. Clear examples would reduce mistakes and unnecessary calls for advice.”

The federation has submitted six worked examples and requested guidance in both Kestrian and French. It also recommends allowing businesses to use existing compliant packaging stocks when the change concerns presentation alone, provided all required consumer information remains accurate and legible.

Ostara workshop helps manufacturers check labels before printing

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
21 September

Thirty-four staff from 22 food businesses attended a label checking workshop in Ostara, organised by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The session focused on common errors that can be caught before packaging goes to print.

Participants worked through fictional product labels covering soups, baked goods and chilled meals. Exercises included checking ingredient order, matching declared weights to product specifications and making storage instructions easy to find.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A second check against the recipe and specification can prevent an expensive reprint. Staff need a clear process for recording who approved a label and which version was sent to the printer.”

The federation distributed a two-page checklist and a sample approval record. The materials reflect current requirements and identify matters still under consultation in the draft labelling guidance. French versions are available to members through the federation’s advice service in Val-Brume.

Packaging levy revision removes duplicate reporting for manufacturers

Media centre · Mara Vennick
17 September

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has welcomed a revised packaging levy proposal published today by the Ministry of Revenue. The revision provides for one reporting return and removes a provision that could have counted some packaging twice.

The proposed rate remains KRN 0.18 per kilogram for the materials covered. The ministry has also added examples showing how manufacturers should record packaging purchased through wholesalers and packaging transferred between factories.

Mara Vennick, policy director, said: “These changes address a practical problem raised in our submission. Businesses can now assess the proposal with a clearer understanding of what they would need to report.”

The federation continues to seek clarification on reusable transport containers and the treatment of returned goods. It has asked members to submit examples with weights and purchase records. The levy remains a proposal, and the federation advises businesses to distinguish the draft requirements from their existing reporting duties.

Summer survey shows steady orders but tighter margins

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
1 September

Food manufacturers reported steady summer orders but continued pressure on margins, according to a survey published today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The survey received responses from 84 businesses employing 12,600 people.

Forty-six per cent said their order volumes were broadly unchanged from the previous three months. Thirty-one per cent reported an increase and 23 per cent a decline. Responses were collected between 10 and 24 August.

Packaging and maintenance were the most frequently reported sources of higher costs. Fifty-eight per cent of respondents said their operating margin had narrowed, while 37 per cent had postponed at least one planned equipment purchase.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Stable orders are welcome, but they do not mean every business is comfortable. Manufacturers in Amberford and Kestrel Bay described particular difficulty finding affordable replacement parts.” The federation cautioned that the voluntary survey represents participating members rather than the entire sector.

Wage talks open with focus on pay and training

Media centre · Devran Pell
9 September

Negotiations on Kestria’s next food manufacturing sector wage agreement opened in Saltmarsh today. The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria is representing 63 employers covered by the agreement, alongside representatives of the Food Production Workers Union.

The opening meeting covered basic pay, shift allowances and access to paid training. The current agreement provides a minimum hourly rate of KRN 14.20 for adult production workers at participating businesses.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “We want an agreement that improves pay and helps factories retain skilled people. Employers also need to understand the full cost, including allowances, before they can make a firm commitment.”

Both negotiating teams exchanged evidence on vacancies, staff turnover and business costs. No pay settlement was reached at the opening meeting. The federation has asked participating employers to check their payroll information so that further discussions use consistent figures for hours, grades and shift patterns.
